title: Introduce authorization-proofing middleware, KMS fence, and canonical audit tags
author: Ethan Park
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to see inconsistent operator-scoped access patterns and opaque KMS provider fallbacks in multi-region customers. Compliance teams asked for stronger proofs that a request was authorized for a region-bound key and consistent audit tagging that surfaces residency and operator assertions. This PR introduces a lightweight authorization-proofing middleware that ties RBAC v2 decisions to KMS routing decisions and produces canonical audit tags to make downstream compliance processing deterministic.

What this change does (summary): - Adds an authorization-proofing middleware that validates operator claims against RBAC v2 decisions and attaches a signed assertion blob used by KMS routing and audit ingestion. - Implements a KMS fence component: a policy-driven allowlist that prevents implicit global KMS fallback when a region claim is present. The fence consults the authorization-proof and rejects or redirects requests to compliant KMS endpoints. - Introduces an audit canonicalizer: normalizes audit metadata (tenant_id, region_pin, operator_scope, assertion_hash, kms_endpoint) into a stable schema consumed by the audit-forwarder and compliance indexer. - Provides a shadow RBAC mapping mode for a staged rollout: the middleware can validate against a shadow mapping and emit metrics without enforcing; feature-flagged enforcement will be enabled after telemetry review.

Key design notes: - Signed assertion blob format is compact (base64 header.payload.sig) and includes operator_id, effective_roles, timestamp, request_nonce, and region_claim. Assertions are signed by the platform signing key (rotated monthly) and verified by the KMS fence and audit pipeline. - KMS fence uses a prioritized policy: (1) explicit customer KMS mapping, (2) region-anchored allowlist, (3) explicit operator consent (when allowed). Global fallbacks are blocked when a region claim exists unless the tenant has an explicit global-allow annotation. - Audit canonicalizer maps heterogeneous audit headers from upstream proxies and SDKs into a 6-field canonical record and emits it to the audit-forwarder with an assertion_hash for de-duplication.

Files changed (high level): - runtime/middleware/auth_proofing.go: middleware implementation, assertion signer/validator hooks. - runtime/kms/fence.go: policy engine and allowlist enforcement. - observability/audit/canonicalizer.go: normalizer and test helpers. - config/policies/kms_fence.yaml: example policy and tenant overrides. - docs/compliance/authorization-proofing.md: design and rollout guide. - tests/integration/auth_proofing_e2e_test.go: end-to-end tests against mock KMS providers and audit-forwarder.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests added for assertion signing and validation (coverage ~92% for new package). - Integration test simulates region-pin present and ensures request is routed to regional KMS and audit record contains canonical tags. - Canary run on Dedicated podset in us-west-2 for 48 hours; metrics collected: assertion-verif-rate, kms-fence-blocks, canonicalization-errors. - We observed ~0.03% additional median latency for requests that require signing (~350us) and no measurable change in 95th percentile for typical text-generation paths.

Rollout plan: - Step 1 (shadow mode): enable middleware in shadow mode (emit metrics and canonical audit tags but do not enforce) across hosted API (default) and Dedicated; collect telemetry for 2 weeks. - Step 2 (canary enforcement): enable enforcement behind feature flag for 5% of traffic on Dedicated; monitor blocked request rate and customer impact. - Step 3 (wider enforcement): after gating on metrics and SRE sign-off, flip enforcement for all new tenants; existing tenants can opt-in while a migration tool annotates tenants with explicit global-allow where required.

Migration and backward compatibility: - Backwards-compatible: when no region claim is present, behavior is unchanged. - For tenants that relied on implicit global KMS fallback, the migration tool will surface affected API keys and suggest per-tenant annotations. - Audit canonicalizer is additive: downstream systems can opt to consume canonical records; older records remain readable.

Operational notes: - Added observability: dashboards for assertion verification failures, kms_fence_block_rate, canonicalization_error_rate, and a lightweight audit-sampling needle for correlation testing. - Security: platform signing key stored in KMS; rotation CI job added to generate rotation notification to security-ops channel. - Emergency bypass: a tenant-level emergency-allow annotation that requires two operator approvals; audited and rate-limited.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of middleware + kms fence + audit canonicalizer - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and rollout guide - [x] Canary validation in Dedicated - [x] Feature flag gating and migration helper

References: ENG-1256 (authorization-proofing epic), PM-78 (compliance requirements), SUP-343 (support case: tenant with implicit global fallback).

release_notes: Add authorization-proofing middleware to tie RBAC v2 decisions to KMS routing; introduce a policy-based KMS fence to prevent implicit global fallback when region claims are present; emit canonical audit tags for deterministic compliance processing. Rollout behind feature flag and shadow mode.
